reconstruction: A deterministic exact-real producer returns actual finite real matrix factors R,Q with A=R*Q and Q*Q.transpose=I, using inner dimension min(m,n), irrespective of deficient rank. In the wide branch it eliminates A.transpose by a specified changing-matrix adjacent-row recurrence and extracts the leading residual block and leading rows of the accumulated orthogonal transform; in the tall branch it returns R=A,Q=I. This is a certified matrix supplier, not merely an existence statement, and not an executable finite-bit factorization or quantum circuit theorem.

public_declarations.name: QuantumBlockEncoding.ConstructiveThinLQ.Factorization
public_declarations.checked_type: {m n : Nat} -> Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) Real -> Nat -> Type
public_declarations.source_signature: structure Factorization {m n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℝ) (r : ℕ) where R : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin r) ℝ; Q : Matrix (Fin r) (Fin n) ℝ; factorization : A = R * Q; orthogonal : Q * Q.transpose = 1
public_declarations.meaning: A data record of two actual matrix fields and two proof fields. A and r are explicit record parameters; m,n are implicit. No triangularity, rank, positive-diagonal, uniqueness, costs, rotations or quantum-register field is present.

public_declarations.name: QuantumBlockEncoding.ConstructiveThinLQ.wideR
public_declarations.checked_type: {m n : Nat} -> m <= n -> Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) Real -> Matrix (Fin m) (Fin m) Real
public_declarations.literal_body: wideR hmn A i k = RectangularGivens.reduced A.transpose (Fin.castLE hmn k) i
public_declarations.meaning: The transpose of the leading m by m residual block of the n by m eliminated transpose, not an arbitrary factor satisfying a relation.

public_declarations.name: QuantumBlockEncoding.ConstructiveThinLQ.wideQ
public_declarations.checked_type: {m n : Nat} -> m <= n -> Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) Real -> Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) Real
public_declarations.literal_body: wideQ hmn A k j = RectangularGivens.transform A.transpose (Fin.castLE hmn k) j
public_declarations.meaning: Exactly the first m rows, in numerical prefix order, of the actual n by n accumulated row-rotation transform.

public_declarations.name: QuantumBlockEncoding.ConstructiveThinLQ.wide_factorization
public_declarations.checked_type: forall {m n : Nat} (hmn : m <= n) (A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) Real), A = wideR hmn A * wideQ hmn A
public_declarations.proof_reconstruction: Let B=A.transpose, U=reduced B and T=transform B. Provider recovery T.transpose*U=B transposes to U.transpose*T=A. Terms indexed by k>=m vanish because U k i=0 for i<m<=k, using reduced_zero_below. Restricting the n-term matrix-product sum to the m-term prefix gives the literal RQ product.

public_declarations.name: QuantumBlockEncoding.ConstructiveThinLQ.wide_orthogonal
public_declarations.checked_type: forall {m n : Nat} (hmn : m <= n) (A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) Real), wideQ hmn A * (wideQ hmn A).transpose = 1
public_declarations.proof_reconstruction: Provider T.transpose*T=I for square T implies T*T.transpose=I. Selecting the first m rows on both sides yields all pairwise row inner products of Q equal to the m by m identity. It does not say Q.transpose*Q=I_n in the strictly wide case.

public_declarations.name: QuantumBlockEncoding.ConstructiveThinLQ.factorOfLE
public_declarations.checked_type: {m n : Nat} -> m <= n -> (A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) Real) -> Factorization A m
public_declarations.literal_body: R:=wideR hmn A; Q:=wideQ hmn A; factorization:=wide_factorization hmn A; orthogonal:=wide_orthogonal hmn A
public_declarations.meaning: Builds one explicit wide-factor record and internally proves its two equations. The caller supplies only the dimension comparison and original matrix.

public_declarations.name: QuantumBlockEncoding.ConstructiveThinLQ.factor
public_declarations.checked_type: {m n : Nat} -> (A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) Real) -> Factorization A (min m n)
public_declarations.literal_body: If m<=n, transport factorOfLE hmn A along min(m,n)=m. Otherwise transport the explicit record R=A,Q=1 with the two simp-proved equations along min(m,n)=n.
public_declarations.meaning: Handles every natural dimension with an actual dimension branch, not Classical.choose of the existing existence theorem. It returns fixed inner dimension min(m,n), not rank(A).

public_declarations.name: QuantumBlockEncoding.ConstructiveThinLQ.factor_correct
public_declarations.checked_type: forall {m n : Nat} (A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) Real), A = (factor A).R * (factor A).Q and (factor A).Q * (factor A).Q.transpose = 1
public_declarations.literal_body: The conjunction of the two proof projections (factor A).factorization and (factor A).orthogonal.
public_declarations.meaning: Certifies this same returned record, with no factorization, orthogonality, nonzero-row, independence, rank or cost certificate supplied by its caller.

record_and_binder_expansion.constructor_checked: Factorization.mk takes implicit m,n,A,r, then actual R:m by r and Q:r by n, then proofs A=RQ and Q*Q.transpose=I_r, and returns Factorization A r.
record_and_binder_expansion.projection_checked: factorization and orthogonal project those two equations from an existing record; they are outputs of factor/factorOfLE, not extra hypotheses of factor_correct.
record_and_binder_expansion.carriers: All scalar entries are arbitrary Real; m,n,r are natural dimensions. No complex adjoint or probabilistic approximate semantics is substituted.
record_and_binder_expansion.wide_shape_condition: hmn:m<=n is an explicit logical dimension condition of wideR,wideQ,their two theorems and factorOfLE, supplying the prefix embedding Fin.castLE. factor removes this restriction by its branch. Its source-relative SOURCE/TYPING/EXCESS classification cannot be decided without the withheld source statement; no author's classification was imported.
record_and_binder_expansion.record_inhabitance: The record type is declared for arbitrary r, but the module does not prove it inhabited for every r. Its actual supplier constructs it only at r=min(m,n).
record_and_binder_expansion.helper_typing: Rectangular sweep carries k+remaining<=M; column sweep carries lo+count<N; Step contains ordered Fin N supports and proof first.val+1=second.val. The producers construct these recursion/index proofs internally.

literal_provider_reconstruction.pairNorm: r(x,y)=sqrt(x^2+y^2)>=0. splitAngle(x,y) is rational zero if r=0, otherwise ExactAngle.real(2*(-arccos(x/r) if y<0 else arccos(x/r))). ExactAngle.eval interprets .real literally. Nonzero r ensures x/r is in [-1,1] as a proved consequence.
literal_provider_reconstruction.rotation_convention: rotateRows A i j theta replaces ordered rows by cos(theta/2)*A_i-sin(theta/2)*A_j and sin(theta/2)*A_i+cos(theta/2)*A_j, fixing every other row. planeMatrix=rotateRows I. The ordered block is [[cos(theta/2),-sin(theta/2)],[sin(theta/2),cos(theta/2)]], matching literal standard RY half-angle radians. No unsigned amplitude or up-to-sign equivalence is used.
literal_provider_reconstruction.elimination: theta=-splitAngle(x,y).eval sends [x,y] to [sqrt(x^2+y^2),0]. At (0,0), theta=0 and the actual full matrix update is identity, without division by zero. Negative y is handled by the signed arccos branch. An unswept final pivot need not be nonnegative.
literal_provider_reconstruction.step_record: AdjacentGivens.Step N has first:Fin N,second:Fin N,adjacent:first.val+1=second.val,angle:Real. distinct follows from adjacency. Step.matrix is the ordered planeMatrix; Step.inverse negates its angle, preserving supports.
literal_provider_reconstruction.bottom_up_column_sweep: For fixed col,lo,count, the positive-count branch first eliminates rows lo+count-1 and lo+count, then recursively sweeps the updated matrix with count-1. Thus adjacent pairs occur bottom-up, ending at lo,lo+1. columnSweepSteps computes each next angle from the changing matrix and has exactly count entries, including zero-angle steps.
literal_provider_reconstruction.rectangular_sweep: For N by M input, sweep starts k=0,remaining=M. When k<N, run columnSweep on column k with lo=k,count=N-1-k, then recurse at k+1 on the updated matrix. For k>=N, skip that column's row sweep but continue the column schedule. remaining=0 returns current A. sweepSteps concatenates the identical current-column log before the updated-matrix tail.
literal_provider_reconstruction.literal_outputs: decompose A=sweepSteps A 0 M; reduced A=sweep A 0 M; transform A=stepsMatrix(decompose A). applySteps executes list head first. stepsMatrix []=I and stepsMatrix(step::rest)=stepsMatrix(rest)*step.matrix, so transform*A=reduced, transform.transpose*transform=I, det(transform)=1, and transform.transpose*reduced=A.
literal_provider_reconstruction.residual_property: UpperPrefix requires earlier columns zero strictly below their numerical diagonals. Existing zero columns remain zero under row mixing, so sweep extends this prefix without a nonzero-pivot assumption. reduced_zero_below applies to every rectangular input.
literal_provider_reconstruction.existing_ThinLQ_role: Read actual ThinLQ. Its wide existence theorem uses gramSchmidtOrthonormalBasis and completion. ConstructiveThinLQ does not select its existential factors; the proof reuses only ThinLQ.sum_prefix_of_zero to restrict a matrix-product sum. An import edge is not proof that the current producer uses basis selection.

shape_rank_sign_cases.strictly_wide: m<n: R is m by m, Q m by n with orthonormal rows. From the literal residual formula R i k=0 when i<k, so the wide R is lower triangular; this is a decoder deduction, not a separately advertised public triangularity theorem.
shape_rank_sign_cases.square: m=n enters the wide branch. No positive-diagonal or determinant-one restriction on A is required. In particular, a 1 by 1 negative entry is retained in R because there is no adjacent row pair to sweep; Q is the 1 by 1 identity.
shape_rank_sign_cases.tall: m>n: R is exactly A (m by n), Q=I_n. Arbitrary tall A need not be lower trapezoidal. Thus the all-shape record is the two-equation contract, not a conventional triangular-R LQ claim for every shape.
shape_rank_sign_cases.deficient_rank: Zero or repeated rows are permitted with no full-rank premise. The orthonormal Q still has min(m,n) rows; R may be singular. This is dimension-thin, not rank-compressed, and not a unique factorization theorem.
shape_rank_sign_cases.zero_matrix: All scheduled elimination pairs are zero, so every computed angle is zero and transform is identity. The wide output is R=0 and Q the first m rows of identity, rather than choosing a basis for only the nonzero rows. This follows from the inspected recurrence; no float replay was used.
shape_rank_sign_cases.m_zero: m=0 enters the wide branch for every n. A.transpose has no columns; decompose is empty, transform=I_n, R is 0 by 0 and Q 0 by n. The two equations use empty-row matrix semantics.
shape_rank_sign_cases.n_zero: n=0,m>0 uses the tall branch with R=A:m by 0 and Q=I_0. m=n=0 uses the wide branch. Empty inner sums and empty identities are valid finite matrix objects; no positive dimension is assumed.
shape_rank_sign_cases.register_boundary: These are numerical Fin-indexed matrices and adjacent row planes, not qubit registers. No little-endian/Gray code, ancilla cleanup, RY/CX instruction list, state-preparation action or Hermite target theorem is asserted by this module.

Signed entries are literal; no positive final diagonal or uniqueness claim.
